title: What did you do?
why: Bert tells the plane story: the woman in the next seat types his name into YouTube, lands on a hit piece, turns the phone around, and asks what he did. He has no answer except that he was trying to make people like him. It is the only moment in the episode where the show's own subject - being clipped out of context - lands as a joke and as a confession at once, and it needs no prior ten minutes. Opens on the question she asks, ends on 'I don't like that about me'.

title: I took some awesome pictures of me
line: I took some awesome pictures of me.
why: 54 years old, alone in the gym at 5 a.m., taking a mirror selfie of his arm in good lighting - and the maintenance guy rides the elevator up into the middle of it. Bert plays the whole thing in real time, including the door closing on him. Pure physical comedy, no reference to anything outside the clip, and the last word is his.

title: Please, leave. I can smell you from here
line: Please, leave. I can smell you from here.
why: A Paris perfume shop: the assistant tries to throw Leanne out, then recognises Bert and reverses every word - 'are you with this evil-minded peasant?' becomes 'come in, this door is open to you'. Twenty seconds, one reversal, and the last line is the shop's, not his. Nothing in it is political, sexual or about anybody real except the two of them, which is what makes it usable when most of this episode is not.

title: Honey, you're fucked
why: A woman at a party tells him what people say about you only matters as much as how you feel about yourself; he asks the obvious follow-up; she delivers the verdict and walks away. Twenty-four seconds, one idea, and the button is somebody else's line - which is why it works as a short.
